subject: Horizon Data — schema & routing follow-up (chat vs completions, streaming)

Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo — schema & streaming questions

Thanks for the demo this morning — helpful overview. A couple of follow-ups from our engineers as we start to sketch the integration: 

1) Chat vs completions: for our use case (multi-turn document Q&A with reranking) are you recommending the chat API or completions API for canonical request/response schema? We care about structured outputs (JSON) and reliable stop behavior.

2) Tokenization & max_tokens: we expect documents up to ~15k tokens; how should we set max_tokens for responses vs context windows? Any recommendations on chunking and overlap to keep reranker accuracy high?

3) Streaming semantics: if we enable streaming to our app, what guarantees do we have around tool-calling/structured output? Will partial tokens break JSON emission, or do you support a streaming mode that emits final structured fields atomically?

4) Auth & SDK: our infra will use server-side SDK with per-request customer routing. What's the best pattern for routing to dedicated vs hosted endpoints and pinning model versions in the SDK config?

Would love a short written recap we can circulate internally. Can Laura join the thread for the SDK/implementation notes?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Engineering Manager
Horizon Data

Ben — great questions, thanks for laying them out. Recap + next steps below so your team has a concise doc to share. Looping in Laura for the implementation details you asked for.

Recap (high level):
- Chat vs completions: for multi-turn doc Q&A we typically recommend the chat endpoint when you need system+assistant+user roles, streaming, and tool-calling in the same session. Completions is fine for single-turn generation or simpler structured outputs.
- Structured output & tool-calling: Redwood supports structured output schemas (JSON) and tool-calling. When you use streaming with tool-calls, we stream tokens but emit tool-invocation events as discrete messages in the stream so you can handle them reliably.
- Tokenization & chunking: given ~15k doc size, we recommend prefixing with a sparse retrieval step (embeddings + retriever) to reduce context to the top-k chunks (~2–4k tokens). We provided guidance on overlap and chunk size (see Laura's notes).
- SDK/routing: use per-tenant config in the SDK to pin model versions; routing policies (latency vs cost) are declarative and can be attached to a route key. Laura will share a sample config.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to share an implementation note with concrete SDK snippets and a sample request/response schema (today EOD).
2) We draft a mutual action plan & SOW outline (I'll send a first cut).
3) Technical sync between your eng leads and our SEs (30–45m) — can you propose slots?

If that sounds right I will send the mutual action plan and attach a quick example schema for chat + tool-calling.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo — schema & streaming questions

Ben / Alex — adding the implementation details you asked for. I'll keep this focused and include code snippets below.

1) Request/response schema (recommended for chat w/ structured output):
- Request: {
  "model": "redwood-chat-4x",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"..."}, {"role":"user","content":"..."}],
  "tool_schema": { "name":"reranker","inputs": ["candidate_ids","scores"], "output":"json" },
  "stream": false /* or true for streaming */
}
- Response (non-stream): a single JSON envelope containing assistant text and tool_invocations: 
  {"assistant_text":"...","tools": [{"name":"reranker","status":"invoked","result": {"top_id":"doc_123", "score": 0.92}}]}

2) Streaming semantics & structured output:
- When stream=true we emit token chunks as they are generated. Tool-calling events are emitted as discrete frames (you will get a JSON control frame that indicates tool invocation and then its results). This prevents partial tokens from breaking structured fields.
- Best practice: subscribe to control frames and buffer final tool results before updating UI. We also support a final "complete" event that contains a verified JSON payload.

3) Tokenization & max_tokens guidance:
- Model context: redwood-chat-4x supports up to 32k context. For 15k source docs do retrieval-first.
- Suggestions: chunk size 1.5–3k tokens, 20% overlap for passage-level QA; set max_tokens_response to 512–1024 depending on answer verbosity.

4) Embeddings & reranker workflow:
- Ingest: create embeddings for passages using the embedding endpoint, store vectors in your vector DB.
- Retrieval: return top-N candidates (we see 10–50 depending on recall needs).
- Rerank: call the model with candidate snippets + user question using a structured prompt to emit a ranked list (assistant outputs JSON array of candidate ids + scores).

5) SDK & auth patterns:
- Use SDK server-side keys per-tenant. In our SDK you can create a RouteConfig object: {"route_key": "horizon-us", "preferred_model": "redwood-chat-4x", "fallback_model": "redwood-complete-3"}.
- For Dedicated customers you set a tenancy header (x-redwood-tenant) and the control plane routes to the correct pool.

Code snippet (Node):
const r = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, routeKey: "horizon-us"});
const res = await r.chat.create({messages, stream: false, tool_schema});

Attachments: sample schema and example payloads attached. Happy to walk through during the sync.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks, nailed the sync slot. Confirmed: 2027-02-23 09:30–10:00 PST for a technical review (invite to follow).

Answers to the two quick items: 
- Streaming ordering: control frames are emitted synchronously in the generation stream before any subsequent token frames that reference them. You will always receive the invocation control frame first, then token frames for tool output (if the tool returns text) and then the tool result frame. That ordering is part of the stream contract.
- Reranker output: you can emit both structured arrays and a short human-readable explanation in the same envelope. Recommendation: put machine-readable data in a top-level "results" array and include "explanation" as an optional field. We will include a schema validator in the SDK to help surface schema mismatches during dev.

I also attached a one-page mutual action plan and a draft SOW for your review — would appreciate any redlines and we can iterate.

See you on the 23rd.

Best,
Tessa
